major_concerns: Emulator realism vs production hardware may limit external validity and claim scope.
Batfish coverage gaps could misclassify semantic errors as passes.
Benchmark size and diversity (300 tasks × vendors/topologies) may be optimistic given wall-clock and annotation costs.
Prompt/style bias: benchmark may favor particular prompt designs or LLM promptability.
required_design_repairs: Specify exact emulator platform (container images, versions) and document known emulator-vs-hardware mismatches.
Include explicit Batfish rule-coverage tests and document cases Batfish cannot verify; provide fallback labeling policy.
Start with a smaller pilot slice (e.g., 50 tasks) to validate pipeline and measure real compute/time before full 300-task run.
Pre-register precise prompt templates, LLM model IDs and hyperparameters, random seeds, and dataset-creation scripts; publish artifacts and hashes.

major_concerns: LLM sensitivity to feedback wording risks confounding the effect attributed to feedback granularity.
Potential cross-condition contamination if model context or cached instructions leak between paired runs.
Verifier-generated 'localized' messages may vary in informativeness across error classes, creating heterogeneity in treatment strength.
required_design_repairs: Define and freeze exact feedback templates and formatting; validate via pre-registered pilot to ensure comparable verbosity/content across tasks.
Enforce strict isolation between paired runs (fresh sessions, controlled seeds) and document session management.
Pre-specify error-class taxonomy and stratification plan; include sensitivity analyses for feedback wording variations.

major_concerns: Learned risk-estimator calibration is a potential single point of failure and may not generalize to new topologies or vendors.
Simulated/emulator stress tests may underrepresent real post-deployment failure modes, biasing stopping-rule comparisons.
Dependence on a single LLM limits external validity of stopping-rule recommendations.
required_design_repairs: Pre-register estimator architecture, training data provenance, hyperparameters, and cross-validation folds; report Brier score and reliability diagrams.
Include holdout topologies/vendors for honest generalization testing; report sensitivity to LLM choice (at least one secondary model or temperature sweep).
Define and report operational utility function used to select Pareto operating point; include conservative thresholds and ablation without learned estimator.

major_concerns: Ethical risk of publishing actionable adversarial examples and exploit techniques; release artifacts must be sanitized.
Adversarial intent construction may not represent adaptive real-world attackers, limiting external validity.
Guarded-policy implementation details (allowlist, sanitization rules) require precise specification to be reproducible and comparable.
required_design_repairs: Produce an explicit ethical-mitigation plan: non-actionable abstractions for adversarial intents, redaction policy, and responsible-release statement.
Pre-register adversarial-intent-generation rules and provide a reproducible (sanitized) generator with seeds; include attacker-strength taxonomy.

Fully specify guardrail implementations (allowlist semantics, sanitization routines) and freeze them in the preregistration; include metrics for benign-block rate and operator-friction quantification.
